priorInsurance.summary: Insurers can't charge you more for having no car insurance when you apply, unless they can show it really predicts claims.
priorInsurance.quote: In determining rates for motor vehicle insurance, an insurer shall not consider the fact that an applicant does not have motor vehicle insurance covering the applicant's motor vehicle at the time of his application for such insurance, unless the insurer has an actuarial justification.

credit.summary: Insurers can use your credit, but can't set your renewal price, or turn you down, based on credit alone.
credit.quote: Base renewal rates for personal insurance of an insured solely upon credit information, without consideration of any other applicable factor independent of credit information;

moreSources.label: 36 Okla. Stat. § 953(2)
moreSources.quote: Deny, cancel or fail to renew a policy of personal insurance solely on the basis of credit information, without consideration of any other applicable underwriting factor independent of credit information

credit.summary: Insurers can use your credit to price a new policy, but can't use it to raise your price at renewal, or to drop you once your policy is more than 60 days old.
credit.quote: Except as provided in subsections (2), (3) and (4) of this section, an insurer may only use rating factors other than credit history or insurance score to rerate the policy at renewal.

moreSources.label: Or. Rev. Stat. § 746.661(1)(a)
moreSources.quote: May not cancel or nonrenew personal insurance that has been in effect for more than 60 days based in whole or in part on a consumer’s credit history or insurance score.

gender.summary: Pennsylvania's top court upheld the state's ban on charging different car insurance prices based on gender.

source.label: Hartford Accident & Indemnity Co. v. Insurance Commissioner, 505 Pa. 571 (1984)

gender.quote: we conclude that the Commissioner's disapproval of Hartford's discriminatory sex-based rates on the ground they were "unfair" and contrary to established public policy was in conformity with section 3(d) of the Rate Act

credit.summary: Insurers can use your credit, but can't hold a missing credit history against you when deciding whether to insure you, unless they show the state it's tied to risk.
credit.quote: Absence of credit information may be used by an insurer for underwriting purposes only if the insurer presents information satisfactory to the director that the absence is related to the risk.

gender.summary: Gender isn't on South Carolina's list of things insurers can't use to set your car insurance price.
